name: who_has_it_worse
shots:
integrated_multimodal_description:
Live-action film footage, vertical 9:16 framing, naturalistic overcast light, realistic detail, natural skin tones, cinematic dark comedy.
[Shot 1] A vertical medium close-up at eye level in an old gloomy cemetery under an overcast gray sky, weathered stone headstones, a damp gravel path, bare trees, soft flat diffuse light, muted desaturated colors. Only Mark (S1), a man in his late thirties with unshaven stubble, tired dark-circled eyes and short messy dark hair, wearing a long dark trench coat over a dark sweater, is in frame, collapsed over an old stone tombstone. At 0.00 seconds Mark hugs the headstone tightly with both arms, eyes closed, tears streaming down his face, shoulders shaking. At 1.50 seconds he lifts his head slightly without letting go, eyes squeezed shut, and Mark (S1) says in a hoarse, trembling, weeping voice: <d>[English] Why did you have to die? You haven't a clue what I've been through since you left... Come back, please!</d> At 7.50 seconds he finishes and presses his wet face back against the cold stone, sobbing quietly, still hugging the headstone. The camera holds this framing until the final frame. All motion happens at natural real-time speed, not slow motion. There are no subtitles, captions, on-screen text, logos or watermarks anywhere in frame.

overall_soundscape:
Heavy sobbing, wind through bare branches, faint distant rooks.

integrated_multimodal_description:
Live-action film footage, vertical 9:16 framing, naturalistic overcast light, realistic detail, natural skin tones, cinematic dark comedy.
[Shot 2] A vertical medium shot in an old gloomy cemetery under an overcast gray sky, weathered stone headstones, a damp gravel path, bare trees, soft flat diffuse light, muted desaturated colors. Mark (S1), a man in his late thirties with unshaven stubble, tired dark-circled eyes and short messy dark hair, wearing a long dark trench coat over a dark sweater, stays on the left side of frame, hunched over the tombstone, hugging it and sobbing quietly. Mark stays silent in this shot and only his shoulders shake. At 2.00 seconds Arthur (S2), a man in his late fifties with grey hair, a short grey beard and a kind lined face, wearing a thick warm brown wool coat and a tweed flat cap, walking along the gravel path from the right edge of frame, hears the crying and stops on the right side of frame. At 4.00 seconds Arthur turns and walks over slowly with a deeply sympathetic, concerned expression and stops beside Mark. At 6.00 seconds Arthur (S2) places a hand near Mark's shoulder and says in a warm, gentle, empathetic voice: <d>[English] Excuse me, sir... are you all right? Was this your wife?</d> Mark (S1) stays silent, his head down against the stone. At 8.50 seconds Arthur waits kindly, hand hovering near Mark's shoulder. The camera holds this framing until the final frame. All motion happens at natural real-time speed, not slow motion. There are no subtitles, captions, on-screen text, logos or watermarks anywhere in frame.

overall_soundscape:
Crunching footsteps on gravel, soft sobbing, a light breeze.

integrated_multimodal_description:
Live-action film footage, vertical 9:16 framing, naturalistic overcast light, realistic detail, natural skin tones, cinematic dark comedy.
[Shot 3] A vertical two-shot in an old gloomy cemetery under an overcast gray sky, weathered stone headstones, a damp gravel path, bare trees, soft flat diffuse light, muted desaturated colors. Mark (S1), a man in his late thirties with unshaven stubble, tired dark-circled eyes and short messy dark hair, wearing a long dark trench coat over a dark sweater, is on the left side of frame with his face against the tombstone, and Arthur (S2), a man in his late fifties with grey hair, a short grey beard and a kind lined face, wearing a thick warm brown wool coat and a tweed flat cap, stands on the right side of frame beside him, hand hovering near Mark's shoulder. For the first 2.00 seconds Mark stays quiet with his head down and Arthur waits. At 2.00 seconds Mark stops crying instantly, slowly straightens up and wipes the tears from his face with the back of his hand; his expression changes from intense sorrow to cold, exhausted bitterness. He does not look at Arthur. At 4.00 seconds Mark (S1) says in a flat, deadpan, sarcastic voice, the same voice as before but dry and calm: <d>[English] No, it's her first husband.</d> Arthur (S2) stays completely silent. At 6.00 seconds Arthur freezes, eyes wide in shock and confusion, mouth slightly open. At 7.50 seconds Mark turns back, buries his face in the tombstone again and lets out a fake sob, while Arthur stays frozen. At 9.00 seconds both hold still. The camera holds this framing until the final frame. All motion happens at natural real-time speed, not slow motion. There are no subtitles, captions, on-screen text, logos or watermarks anywhere in frame.

overall_soundscape:
A crow caws in the distance, then an awkward silence.
